CANONICAL_NAME.value: Parametrizable priority / round-robin arbiter with priority encoder (Verilog, Alex Forencich, verilog-axi)

VERSION.value: alexforencich/verilog-axi master rtl/arbiter.v + rtl/priority_encoder.v as fetched 2026-09-12

value.lineage: The two-module arbiter used across Forencich's open FPGA IP (AXI, Ethernet, PCIe): a priority encoder plus an arbiter that can be fixed-priority or round-robin, with block-on-acknowledge or block-on-grant policies -- a SMALL DECISION MECHANISM (who gets the bus this cycle) with exposed state (mask, grant, grant_encoded). Rival to the freecores rr-arbiter already in the vault.

value.built_to: decide each cycle which of several requesters owns a shared resource, either by fixed priority or in rotation
value.pressure: simultaneous requests for one bus; the fairness/latency trade-off between priority and rotation
value.success_means: exactly one grant per cycle when any request is present; round-robin serves every persistent requester within PORTS cycles

value.failure_condition: starvation of a low-priority requester (fixed mode) or two simultaneous grants

ANCESTRY.value: The two-module arbiter used across Forencich's open FPGA IP (AXI, Ethernet, PCIe): a priority encoder plus an arbiter that can be fixed-priority or round-robin, with block-on-acknowledge or block-on-grant policies -- a SMALL DECISION MECHANISM (who gets the bus this cycle) with exposed state (mask, grant, grant_encoded). Rival to the freecores rr-arbiter already in the vault.

cut.note: a grant decision in two modules: a logarithmic-depth priority encoder built as a tree of two-input stages (each stage says 'is either half valid' and 'which half wins'), and an arbiter that instantiates the encoder twice, once on the raw requests and once on the requests masked to those ABOVE the last grant, so that round-robin is 'take the masked winner if any, else the unmasked one' and the mask is rebuilt from the winner; two hold policies keep a grant until the request drops or until an acknowledge arrives

provenance.grade_basis: Techne FOSSIL_PACKET.json PROVENANCE_GRADE where issued, else the record's handoff string mapped (populated per R34; Harmonia may re-grade)

organs.human_name: priority_encoder.v: LEVELS = clog2(WIDTH); stage_valid[l][n] = |stage_valid[l-1][2n+1:2n]; stage_enc[l] = (upper half valid ? {1, upper index} : {0, lower index}) or the LSB-first mirror; output_unencoded = 1 << output_encoded
organs.mechanism: the input is padded to a power of two; level 0 pairs adjacent bits and records whether either is set and which one wins (MSB or LSB by parameter); each higher level pairs two lower results, ORs their validity and prepends one index bit choosing the winning half; the top level yields the index of the highest-priority set bit in log2(WIDTH) gate delays, and a one-hot decode of it
organs.output: valid, an index, a one-hot mask
assumptions: log-depth is worth the generate-loop complexity for wide vectors; the LSB/MSB priority choice is a parameter, not a rewrite
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: a wide-port arbiter that meets timing
organs.human_prior: the tree priority encoder (any digital design text)

organs.human_name: arbiter.v: priority_encoder_inst on request; priority_encoder_masked on request & mask_reg; if ARB_TYPE_ROUND_ROBIN: masked winner if masked_request_valid else raw winner; mask_next = all-ones shifted past the winner's index (direction by ARB_LSB_HIGH_PRIORITY)
organs.mechanism: the mask register holds ones for every port strictly after the last granted port in priority order; each cycle two encoders run in parallel, one on the raw requests and one on the masked requests; if any masked request exists its winner is granted (the next port after the last grant that is requesting), otherwise the raw winner is granted (wrap-around); the mask is then set to the ports after the new winner; with round-robin off, the raw encoder's winner is granted (fixed priority)
assumptions: fairness is 'the next requester after the last served'; two encoders in parallel cost less latency than one encoder plus a rotate
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: fair arbitration at the same depth as fixed priority
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: a port that requests only when it is not next can still starve under adversarial timing (the classic limit of masked round-robin); no weighting
organs.human_prior: the mask-based round-robin arbiter (a standard bus-arbiter idiom)

organs.human_name: arbiter.v: ARB_BLOCK && !ARB_BLOCK_ACK && (grant_reg & request) -> hold; ARB_BLOCK && ARB_BLOCK_ACK && grant_valid && !(grant_reg & acknowledge) -> hold
organs.mechanism: with blocking on and acknowledge off, the current grant is held as long as the granted port keeps requesting (a transaction-length hold); with acknowledge on, the grant is held until the granted port raises acknowledge (a handshake); without blocking the arbiter re-decides every cycle
assumptions: consumers of a grant need either a level (request stays high) or a pulse (ack) to finish a transfer; both are common in the author's AXI and Ethernet IP
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: one arbiter serves both handshake styles
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: a granted port that never acknowledges holds the bus forever (no timeout)

rejected_cuts.evidence: the encoder, the round-robin mask and the hold policy are separately parameterised

pressures.condition: N ports request a shared resource; the organism grants one per cycle; the score is the worst-case wait of any continuously requesting port (fairness), the logic depth of the decision, and the absence of interrupted transactions
pressures.resource_or_constraint: one clock cycle; a few registers
pressures.failure_condition: starvation of a low-priority port, a decision deeper than the clock allows, or a grant withdrawn mid-transaction
pressures.world_punishes: fixed priority under load (starvation); a rotate-and-encode chain (depth); re-deciding every cycle (interruption)
pressures.world_rewards: a tree encoder, a masked second encoder, a hold policy
pressures.observable_consequence: worst-case wait per port under all-ports-requesting for fixed vs round-robin; logic depth from synthesis at WIDTH 4, 16, 64; interrupted transfers with blocking off vs on
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: a time-slot scheduler (fair but wastes idle slots)
pressures.cheat_control: an organism with a global schedule must show zero idle grants and perfect fairness; fixed priority must starve the last port under saturation; round-robin must bound the wait by N: the world must show all three
pressures.purpose_separated_from_pressure: PURPOSE: bus and crossbar arbitration in open FPGA IP (Forencich 2014-2021)
